best_for: People who read, mark up, fill in and sign PDFs and never change the text.
description:
Acrobat Reader is Adobe's free PDF app. Adobe created the PDF format more than 30 years ago, and Reader opens files with their fonts and layout kept as the author made them. It is free to use with no subscription.

On a form with fields, you type into the boxes or pick from drop-down lists, and Reader can suggest answers it saved before. On a plain PDF with no fields, you can type straight onto the page. You can sign by drawing, typing your name or uploading a picture of your signature. Sticky notes, highlights and strikethrough let you leave comments, and Share sends the file to people who can view and comment without signing in.

points.title: Cannot edit the text
points.text: Adobe states that text and image editing is not available in Reader. If you need to change wording inside a PDF, Reader is the wrong tool.

points.title: Where the paid line sits
points.text: Acrobat Pro was listed at USD 19.99 a month or USD 239.88 a year, and Acrobat Studio at USD 24.99 a month or USD 299.88 a year. We did not confirm where export, combine and page tools fall.

points.title: This is the 64-bit build
points.text: This listing is the 64-bit Windows package, and its installer sets Reader up for all users on the PC.

points.title: Windows and Mac versions differ
points.text: The Windows listing is at 26.003.22075 and the Mac cask at 26.001.21662, so the two are on different release steps.

points.title: Windows and Mac only
points.text: Adobe's Reader page covers Windows, macOS and phones, and no Linux desktop version. The Acrobat web app works in a browser.

points.title: A long Windows history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps over a hundred past versions, but the Mac cask carries only the current one.
